clauses.reason: Executive Order 10878, signed 1960-05-23, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railroad Company and other carriers represented by the Western Carriers’ Conference Committee and certain of their employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10878_Emergency_board_created_by_EO_10878_May_23_1960_25_FR_4575_Chicago_Rock_Island_and_Pa_d70cbe5acb.txt) gives the date 1960-07-08 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1960-07-08, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1960-08-07, and the order was functionally spent on 1960-08-07 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10878 at character offset 10751 as entry 61 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 61 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
EO 10878 is a Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency-board order with provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed the order’s identity from its heading and number, and confirmed a single-clause inventory. It has no own-terms end. The only held instrument that revokes it is EO 12553 (1986-02-25), which I read; the report date and the end of the status-quo period are disclosed spent facts, not ends. The searches chosen (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) carry no coverage warning and show no hit for this order that contradicts the ending.
